Chapter 6: The Courage to Tell the Truth
Honesty—now, isn’t that a double-edged sword? Most of us crave the chance to be seen for who we really are, to drop the mask and just say what’s true. But at the same time, there’s that nagging fear: What if people judge us? What if they walk away or just don’t get it? The risk of rejection can keep even the bravest among us quiet.
But here’s the thing—if we want to grow, to heal, and to step forward in our faith, we’ve got to be willing to tell the truth. First, to ourselves. Then to the people around us.
Picture this: It’s late at night. Someone’s sitting alone at the kitchen table, wrestling with a secret that’s been eating away at them for years. The silence feels heavy. Fear is almost paralyzing. But hiding has become too painful. So, with trembling hands, they pick up the phone or maybe write a letter, and finally, the truth spills out.
Relief comes quickly—like a weight’s been lifted and you can finally breathe again. But so does vulnerability. There’s no guarantee someone’s going to understand, or that forgiveness is coming. Still, there’s this unmistakable sense of freedom.
In a small church community, honesty turns into a kind of currency. People gather in circles, sharing stories—stories of failure, hope, dreams that fell apart and dreams they picked up again. There’s laughter, and sometimes, yeah, there are tears. But always a sense of solidarity. No one’s pretending to have it all together.
When we tell the truth—when we name the hard stuff out loud—we make room for grace.
Of course, being honest isn’t always easy. Sometimes, the truth makes people uncomfortable. Old habits of avoiding or denying things might come creeping back. But, over time, telling the truth becomes a habit. It’s a way of life. And you start to see that healing only happens when we drag our wounds into the light, trusting that even the messiest parts of our story could be met with a little compassion.
For a lot of us, finding the courage to be honest is the first real step toward change. It’s that moment we stop reading from the old script and start writing a new one. The journey’s ongoing, and yeah, the risks are real. But just imagine the rewards: freedom, connection, and the chance to finally be known for who you really are.
